issues.failure_explanation: The estimate in Lemma lem:p-est is only δ^2 ∑ ||π_j||^p ≤ c. This gives ||π||_{L^p} ≤ C δ^{-1/p}, since ||π||_{L^p}^p = δ ∑ ||π_j||^p. Because ξ is the primitive of π, ||ξ||_{L^p} ≤ T ||π||_{L^p} ≤ C δ^{-1/p}, which blows up as δ→0. For example, π_j = δ^{-1/2} satisfies the estimate for p=8/7 in d=3, but ξ(t)=t δ^{-1/2} has unbounded L^p norm. Thus the claimed uniform bound on ξ^k is not implied by Lemma lem:p-est.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must provide a stronger pressure estimate, e.g. δ ∑ ||π_j||^p ≤ c, or otherwise control the primitive ξ^k uniformly, likely by exploiting the discrete divergence-free property to remove the time-derivative term from the pressure estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence proof for the pressure term fails, so the limit passage in the discrete equation and hence the main convergence theorems are not established as written.
issues.title: Pressure primitive bound does not follow from the pressure estimate
issues.why_classification: The missing pressure bound invalidates a central step of the convergence proof and requires a new nontrivial pressure estimate or alternative argument, affecting the main theorems.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Due to the convective term, the velocity function is not an admissible test function for the three dimensional time-dependent Navier--Stokes equations. For this reason, only an energy inequality rather than an equality is available.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper itself states that only an energy inequality is available for the 3D time-dependent Navier--Stokes equations because the velocity is not an admissible test function. The claimed energy identity would require justification of the energy equality, which is not established for the weak solutions constructed here (they only have u ∈ L^{8/3}(I;L^4) in 3D, not the L^4(I;L^4) condition sufficient for energy equality). The proof in Step 4 is only sketched and does not prove the required convergence of the convective term to allow equality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either replace the energy identity by an energy inequality and adjust the Minty argument accordingly, or impose and verify additional regularity (e.g. u ∈ L^4(I;L^4)) that justifies energy equality.
issues.overall_effect: The energy identity overclaim invalidates the Minty-type identification of the nonlinear boundary term for r>2 and hence the antisymmetric Nitsche convergence theorem.
issues.title: Energy identity contradicts the stated limitation to an energy inequality
issues.why_classification: The false energy identity is used to prove a key limsup inequality for the r>2 convergence result; repairing it requires a new argument or a major restriction of the claimed regime.
